text:
- It reads the hook commands from `<plugin-dir>/hooks/hooks.json` (the `--plugin-dir` that `run` passes; Claude Code hooks shape) and runs every `type:"command"` entry for the event. `hook_commands(…, tool)` evaluates a group's `matcher` against a tool-bearing payload's `tool_name` (landed with chunk 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id, whose PreToolUse group carries `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`); the relayed dialog fixtures carry `tool_name`. An absolute `command` is spawned directly with its `args`, never through a shell or a PATH lookup. A non-absolute `command` is never run, and its receipt reads `command_absolute:false, ran:false`.
 The payload on stdin is the bytes of `<fixtures>/<cli-version>/<Event>.<variant>.json`; for UserPromptSubmit only the top-level `prompt` key is set (the object re-serialised, the fixture's trailing newline kept, so the recorded prompt yields the recorded bytes); under `--resume <id>` the SessionStart fired at launch is the set's recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` when the set holds it (2.1.287, 10 key names, since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows; `launch_variant`, proved by `fake_resume_launches_on_the_recorded_resume_variant_when_the_set_holds_one` and `fake_agent_resume_launches_on_the_recorded_resume_variant`), else its recorded `SessionStart.default` payload (a set without the variant, 2.1.288), with `source` set to `resume` and `session_id` set to the id given (with `--fork-session` beside it, to the compiled id `0f0e0d0c-0b0a-4908-8706-050403020100`), the trailing newline kept (the operator's word at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive's P4); no other payload is built save the compact replay's `SessionStart.compact-1` under `--framing`, whose `session_id` is set to the last SessionStart the agent fired, and without `--resume` every other payload is the recorded bytes; a `paste-<n>` variant replayed under `--framing` goes to the hook with its bytes unchanged, its recorded `prompt` kept. Given `--settings <file>` it reads that file's `statusLine.command` and splits it on ASCII white space; only when `--statusline-stdin <file>` is given too and the command is absolute does it run the command, with that file's bytes on stdin, and write a `statusline` receipt (landed at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through).
 Under `--framing`, with `--settings <file>` naming an absolute `statusLine.command` and no `--statusline-stdin`, it replays the set's `StatusLine.default-1.json` after the launch SessionStart's hooks and `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` once after the first Stop, at the end of that turn after the turn screen is written; the one word exactly `"$0"` is handed over as `/bin/sh`, the command spawned directly, never through a shell; each writes a `statusline` receipt with `stdin_hex`; a relative command is receipted `command_absolute:false, ran:false` and never run; a set without the variants fires nothing; no option is added (since chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows).

text:
- Modes: `--suppress-prompt-submit`, `--local-command-mode` (a `/`-prefixed prompt fires no UserPromptSubmit), `--inject-harness-turn` (one gated step before the script that fires a `<task-notification>`-prefixed prompt with `origin:"harness"`), `--exit-no-eof` (a bounded re-exec holder keeps the child's console / PTY slave open for 10 s — not viola's stdout — writes a `hold` receipt, and on Unix spawns in its own process group), `--report-version <ver>`, print mode `-p <prompt>` / `--print <prompt>` (it writes its start receipts, fires SessionStart/default, UserPromptSubmit/default with `prompt` set, Stop/default and SessionEnd/default from the fixture set, prints `ok` on stdout and exits 0; never raw, never reading stdin — the mode `viola verify`'s print probe drives against the fake agent in CI; `DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` is 2.1.287, the recorded set's version, so the default `--version` answer is `2.1.287 (Claude Code)`, and the harness's `viola_e2e::harness::boot::DEFAULT_CLI_VERSION` — the `boot --cli-version` default — is the same), thirteen argv options (no env; the count's rule is architecture's list of them), two of them for the statusline tests, `--settings <file>` and `--statusline-stdin <file>` (the settings command runs with both options, only when it is absolute, with the stdin file's bytes on its stdin, and under `--framing` without `--statusline-stdin` with the set's recorded `StatusLine` variants), and the eleven that follow, nine of them for verify's interactive runs and their tests
 — `--trusted-root <DIR>` (an ancestor walk, both paths canonicalised), `--screens` (writes `Screen.modal` when untrusted, no hook fired, or `Screen.ready` when trusted, SessionStart as before: a clear, then rows joined by CRLF) , `--turn-stop` (a submit fires UserPromptSubmit, then Stop, then writes `Screen.turn`), `--dialogs` (Runs C and D: a pasted compiled dialog prompt replays its recorded `<stem>-<n>` variants in claim order — a call's PreToolUse first; with no decision its PermissionRequest; a decision from either fires its PostToolUse), `--framing` (Run B: a pasted compiled paste text fires its recorded `paste-1` / `paste-2` / `paste-3` UserPromptSubmit variant with its bytes unchanged, a new stem reached through `ledger::framing_stem` with no option added, the probed `/clear` fires the recorded `clear-1` SessionEnd then SessionStart and no UserPromptSubmit, and the probed `/compact` the recorded `SessionStart.compact-1` with the last fired SessionStart's `session_id` and no UserPromptSubmit; and, with an absolute `--settings` status line command, the set's `StatusLine.default-1.json` after the launch SessionStart and `StatusLine.rate-limits-1.json` once after the first Stop; a set without a variant fires nothing for it, and without the option the agent echoes the typed text) and the two test-only holds `--stop-receipt-hold-ms <n>` (capped at 1 000 ms, a hold of the Stop hook's receipt that forces a race window open; `fire` reports whether a hook printed) and `--paste-hint-ms <ms>` (capped at 10 000 ms;
 with `--framing`, after the long text's replay and its Stop the screen is cleared and `Screen.turn` is drawn only after the hold, which forces open the window in which a real CLI shows its paste hint) and the test-only screen switch `--tag-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: after the turn of the compiled tag-like paste, and after no other turn, the agent draws `Screen.<phase>.json` of its set in place of `Screen.turn`; a missing file draws nothing), the test-only screen switch `--long-turn-screen <phase>` (with `--framing` and `--turn-stop`: after the long paste's turn alone, after its Stop, the agent draws `Screen.<phase>.json` of its set in place of `Screen.turn`; parse cases `opts_long_turn_screen_takes_the_phase_it_names_alone` and `opts_long_turn_screen_defaults_to_none`), and two for `viola revive`'s tests and, under the fake agent, verify's Run E, `--resume <id>` (the launch SessionStart reports source `resume` and that id) and `--fork-session` (beside `--resume`, the compiled fork id; alone it changes nothing); every wrapper boot in `tests/support` and the harness passes `--screens --trusted-root <cwd>` (`Wrapper::boot_untrusted` passes no root), and a test whose fake agent writes another screen (e.g. `--vt100-panic-bytes`) keeps its own verdict — and unknown arguments ignored. Beside the options the agent takes two mode words. `statusline-echo`, landed at chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through: it prints its output and files its stdin, and its exit is the code after the marker path.
 `agents` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board): a first word `agents` answers `agents --json` from files beside its exe (`agents-mode`, `agents-rows.json`, and the live `sessions/<pid>.json` registry: a row written just before its launch SessionStart fires, its `cwd` the launch fixture's recorded `cwd`, `~` without one; a dead or reused pid skipped through one `viola_state::liveness::start_times()` read), built on the recorded `Agents.recorded-1.json`; no option and no env are added; units `agents_output_*`, `live_sessions_skip_a_dead_or_reused_pid`, `launch_session_replays_the_recorded_id_and_cwd` and `planted_rows_of_a_malformed_rows_file_are_none`. The `--resume` launch payload is recorded since chunk 2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows: Run E recorded `SessionStart.resume-1.json` live on 2.1.287, and the launch builds on it there; the rewritten default payload stays only for a set without the variant. As measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, a live reading on `claude` 2.1.287 holds 10 key names where the rewritten payload holds 5 (`cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `session_id`, `source`, `transcript_path`; the five more are `context_tokens`, `estimated_cache_write_usd`, `prompt_cache_likely_expired`, `scratchpad_dir`, `seconds_since_last_response`; as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, `evidence/live-revive.md`). The recorded variant holds those 10 key names, and the `--resume` shape is the `resume-session` ledger row. `--vt100-panic-bytes` is built (with confirmed `send`'s chaos case): after its `start` receipt it writes `e4 b8 ad` once to its terminal and receipts nothing new. Its bytes are measured: under a 24×1 PTY a wide character (`e4 b8 ad`) panics vt100 0.16.2, so no new env seam is needed (as measured at chunk 2026-10-04-readiness-gate-and-timing-constants). `--report-version` changes only the `--version` answer.
 Fixture replay still follows `--cli-version` / `--fixtures`, so a home stamped for a fixture version can run an unlisted reported version (Path 7).
 The `--exit-no-eof` holder's re-exec mode `--hold-stdout-internal` (it sleeps 10 s and writes nothing) is also spawned directly by the server-identity impostor cases (`tests/security_negatives_server_identity.rs`, `tests/hook_fail_open.rs`) as the live process whose pid the impostor's snapshot records, killed and reaped by each file's `Held` `Drop` guard.

Every workflow (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`) has `permissions: {}` at the top and `contents: read` per job. Every `uses:` is SHA-pinned; zizmor `unpinned-uses` is the assertion. Tools are installed with taiki-e/install-action v2.87.19 (SHA-pinned) as `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-llvm-cov@0.9.1,cargo-mutants@27.1.0,cargo-deny@0.20.2`; `windows-mutants.yml` installs `tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.146,cargo-mutants@27.1.0` with the same action, and `tests/contract_windows_mutation_scope.rs` asserts those two pins equal the `test` job's `tool:` line. hyperfine 1.20.0, cargo-modules 0.27.0 and zizmor 1.30.1 are installed with `cargo install --locked <crate>@<version>` in the jobs that invoke them. G2 (`scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`, in the `test` and `perf` jobs), `scripts/orphans-check.sh` (`lint`) and `scripts/release-check.sh` (`release`) use the runner-provided `jq`, never installed: the `test` and `perf` jobs presence-check it (`jq --version`) and all three scripts refuse with `tool-missing: jq`. ripgrep 15.2.0, the G1/G3 tool, comes from `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh` (pinned, checksum-verified official release) in the `lint` job. cargo-fuzz 0.13.2 is installed with `cargo install --locked`, only in the `fuzz-replay` and nightly `fuzz` jobs, with the channel from `fuzz/rust-toolchain.toml`. See §3 Bootstrap `ci-tool-install`. rustfmt and clippy come from `rust-toolchain.toml` `components`, installed by the `rustup toolchain install` step (no toolchain action; the MSRV and fuzz jobs, which need a different toolchain, name theirs). cargo-deny and zizmor run as the pinned CLIs above; cargo-deny-action and zizmor-action are not used, so each tool has exactly one version source.
 The local pre-push gate runs natively on the Linux dev host and installs nothing: its `tools` stage checks the host's `cc`, the `rust-toolchain.toml` channel, the pins it parses from the `test` job's `tool:` line (cargo-nextest 0.9.146, cargo-mutants 27.1.0, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, as read on the Linux dev host 2026-10-04), refusing a missing or off-pin tool with `tool-missing` / `tool-pin-mismatch` — so ci.yml stays the one version source. No provisioning script remains. cargo-deny 0.20 takes `--config <path>` as a global option before the subcommand; `check -c` is rejected (as measured on cargo-deny 0.20.2, dev host, 2026-09-24).
No workflow (`ci.yml`, `nightly.yml`, `windows-mutants.yml`) has a `concurrency:` block: a concurrency group cancels pending runs even with `cancel-in-progress: false`, which would drop a push's `always()` gate and upload chain. zizmor's pedantic `concurrency-limits` finding is declined and stays visible (3 low, one per workflow; zizmor 1.30.1 on the dev host, 2026-10-04).

subject: gate-perf
text:
- **Perf session:** `--perf` then boots ONE session through its `PerfSession` seam (`boot::boot` / `cleanup::cleanup`; the harness's own tests stand in for both): `perf-<harness pid>`, a `builder` instance, `BootOptions { bin_dir: target/perf/release, build: false, stamp: false }`, its home under `target/e2e-home/` (boot step 2), unstamped, so the `pre-tool-use` row times the unverified-CLI path (`hook.dialog` → `null` at once). Each row's synthetic payload (string fields only, the tests-owned content canary in content fields; no recorded fixture exists yet) is written to `target/agent-run/<session>/payload-<hook>.json` and fed through `--input`; hyperfine runs with the repo root as cwd and `VIOLA_NAME=builder` / `VIOLA_DIR=<perf home>/instances/builder` set, so every timed hook takes the real logging and channel path, never the no-instance no-op (obs-plan §10 obs-overhead row) — as measured at chunk 2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate: a kept-home run held 132 `hook-decision` lines with no fallback `detail` and 33 wrapper events per row. Each row's stale export is removed first. After the last row and **before** `cleanup`, `--perf` asserts the home's role files (`diagnostics/*.ndjson` without `detail-*`) hold no `event:"panic"` line, with no seam exemption, because a hook panic exits 0 and hyperfine cannot see it; a panic line fails `panic`. Then `cleanup` (`keep_homes` = `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` exactly `1`) must report `ok:true`. A failed build (`build`), boot (`boot: <reason>`), row (the hook's name), panic check or cleanup turns suite `perf` red with the failure named, never a missing or skipped row.
 Every timed hook also makes its server check (the peer pid and its OS start time against the one snapshot read) before its first frame; with the check in the timed path the hook rows read `max` 2.2–2.4 ms over 30 runs each on the Linux dev host, as measured at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-26-server-verification-before-any-frame/report.md` (Outcome, `run --perf`).
